target_customer: Startup founders and small businesses that plan budgets, hiring and runway
problem: Founders model cash, hiring and runway in spreadsheets, which are error prone and hard to share.

founders.name: Andy Su
previous_startups: inDinero (YC S10, co-founded with Jessica Mah)

technical_complexity.rationale: Connectors to accounting and banking data plus planning dashboards are standard SaaS engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Founders keep financial models in the tool, but spreadsheets and other planning tools were substitutes.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Brex bought Pry in April 2022 for about $90M, its largest acquisition to date.

market_need_then: Seed funded startups had new cash to plan, and 2021 saw heavy startup funding, but demand evidence beyond press coverage was not gathered.

branding.domain_note: Started at pry.co; YC page says now at prune.com, and pry.co redirects to brex.com after the acquisition.

identity.visual_style: Dashboards pitched as a Figma of finance

rebrands.why: YC page says now at prune.com, reason not sourced

brand_strength.rationale: Short memorable name and TechCrunch coverage, but no mascot or community evidence.

outcome_analysis: Pry was built by a repeat YC founder, Andy Su, raised a $4.2M seed in August 2021 and had about ten people when Brex bought it in April 2022 for roughly $90M, its largest deal at the time. A small team, a clear founder audience and a strategic fit with Brex's spend management produced a fast, high-multiple exit.
notes: pry.co redirects to brex.com (not fetched). TechCrunch says the company raised just over $4M in total, consistent with the $4.2M seed; CB Insights shows 4.33M over 6 rounds. The Prune rename comes only from the YC page. No dated 2021 competitor sources found (search returned 2026 pages), so the list is empty.
